Resolves #21379

`Neo.desktop.Container#appWindowConfigs` gives each app window its own config, keyed by app id. An entry takes any window config, such as a size, plus `view`: the app's content, as a class or as a loader, resolved on the app's first open and shown as the window's one item. The window manager awaits the window config together with the window class, before the open's ticket check. The open is listed before either loader runs, since both are the consumer's code: a loader that opens its own app joins the open, and one that closes the app ends it, so the next open loads afresh. An open that ends during either load therefore creates no window, and a failed load lets the next open retry.

`examples/desktop/basic` is the first consumer: Notes edits a note, Calculator calculates and Music lists its tracks, each at its own size. The example's placeholder `AppWindow` goes. #21353 builds the demo's eleven apps on the same seam.

Evidence: L3 (unit arms; the example's e2e arm in Chromium; live frames of `dev` and of this head) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-3 unit, AC-4 and AC-5 e2e, AC-6 frames and cold look). Residual: none.

Change class: capability (`feat`). agent-preflight: not hosted here; the pre-commit and pre-push guards ran.

## Cold look

Readers without context ran one at a time. Each saw one neo-dark frame and answered #21348's three questions: what is this screen, how much does it look like a finished product a visitor would trust (1 to 10), and what is its weakest point.

| Frame | Grade | Weakest point |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` (control) | 3 | "nothing inside the windows is real": one placeholder sentence each |
| this head | 6 | the window layout (the calculator against the music window's edge), no player or selected row in Music, the title-bar controls "crude" |
| this head | 6 | the window layout, the empty strip under the last row, the title-bar controls "a bare underscore, a boxy maximize, an 'x' box" |

Both after readers named the window glyphs, which #21378 redraws. A read of an earlier head, also 6, named three things that changed before the final frame: track numbers restarting per album, near-black grid rows against the glass windows, and a gap under the rows. The calculator's place is the probe's drag, not the app.

## Deltas from ticket
- The view's item takes `flex: 1`, so it fills the window's body (a vbox).
- In `WindowManager.spec.mjs`, the arm for an open that ends after its window exists now closes the app from the window's own construction. `windowConfig`, its old hook, now runs before the ticket check and can no longer stand for "after creation". The behaviour the arm pins is unchanged.
- Notes and Music theme through their components' own CSS variables (`--textfield-*`, `--grid-*`), set from the desktop's window tokens, so they sit on the window glass in both neo themes and no rule competes with the components' own.

## Test Evidence
- Calculator, live in Chromium: `12+30=` gives 42, `.1+.2=` 0.3, `7÷0=` Error, `2+3×4=` 20 (one operation at a time), `50%` 0.5, `123⌫` 12, `9−10=` −1, and after Error a digit starts fresh.
- First-open loading, live: after a reload neither app's CSS is requested, and `Calculator.css` arrives with the app's first open. The view modules load in the App worker, outside the tab's network log; the AC-2 arm pins them.
- The three `WindowManager.spec.mjs` arms for a config callback fail at d8ebce43e3, in a base worktree: the reentrant open recurses until the stack overflows, the open after the close joins the ended one, and the class load's rejection goes unhandled. All 40 desktop unit arms pass at b51e3a0e44.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

- **Rationale**: No premise-conflict row fires. The desktop's real windows are a clear improvement, and per-app configuration belongs to the consumer's catalog. Awaiting window configuration introduces an admission race before the manager records its in-flight request.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Notes, Calculator and Music make the desktop window ownership visible. The before/after pairs show the intended change in both themes.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

- **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #21379, #21198, the current window-manager admission and task ownership, and the prior exact-head review evidence from #21348. Targeted Memory Core recall did not supersede the ticket's ordering contract.
- **Expected Solution Shape:** Resolve per-app content for the first open while preserving one shared flight per app, cancellation, and next-open retry. Install that flight before consumer loaders can reenter the manager.
- **Patch Verdict:** The view/size seam fits at `d8ebce43e337ecf587c5f34cd519549d2e155468`. New synchronous callback entry before flight publication breaks the existing guarantee.
- **Premise Coherence:** Verify before assert. The focused replay checks the first callback boundary before any loader settles.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** I imported the Git-blob-verified WindowManager into the existing Neo test setup. A `windowConfig` callback synchronously reopening the same id ran twice and constructed two distinct windows for one task. A callback that closes the app before returning a deferred config caused an immediate reopen to join the canceled flight and return null. A later open could retry. A separate exact-source replay also showed an unhandled class-loader rejection when the config callback throws before the `Promise.all` handlers attach.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** The normal deferred tests support the default path. The claim that the second open always joins the first needs the reentrant control.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

- **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: A cached open must install its identity before evaluating consumer code that can call back into the manager.

### 🎯 Close-Target Audit

**Findings:** #21379 is an enhancement leaf. AC-2 and AC-3 remain open for synchronous callback entry and invalidation. The named demo consumption stays with #21353.

### 📑 Contract Completeness Audit

**Findings:** `openApp` calls `#createWindow` before inserting the returned promise into `#windows`. The newly concurrent config callback runs as a `Promise.all` argument during that call, so it executes before the slot exists. The old config callback ran after the awaited window-class load.

### 🪜 Evidence Audit

**Findings:** The authored browser tests cover app sizes, live views and note persistence. Exact-module probes used real manager code with mounting substituted, and observe distinct returned windows, tasks and retry behavior. The release examples remain within the intended scope.

### 📸 Before/After Audit

**Findings:** Better. In both pinned themes the windows have recognizable real content. The glyph work and the eleven demo apps have existing follow-up scope.

### N/A Audits — 📡 🔗

N/A across listed dimensions. This extends an existing desktop seam and its live example.

### 🧪 Test-Evidence & Location Audit

**Findings:** [Exact-head unit tests](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44364542182/job/135020176177) passed. The deferred loader tests start their second open once the caller already owns the flight. A synchronous callback at the start boundary is the adverse control missing from those tests.

### 📋 Required Actions

To proceed with merging, please address the following:

- [ ] Register the same-app open before invoking either user-provided loader, and observe both loader failures through the same flight (AC-2 and AC-3). On this head a synchronous config callback can open the same app twice, or close its own open and leave an immediate reopen joining the stale request. If the config throws synchronously while the class load rejects, that class rejection can go unobserved. Add controls for reentrant same-id open and an immediate reopen after invalidation, preserving failed-load retry and one task per owned window.
